name: A Length-Extrapolatable Transformer
problem: A transformer trained on short texts degrades sharply when evaluated on longer ones, and the usual framing (interpolate vs extrapolate positions) does not explain WHY: it lacks a quantity that predicts which variant will survive length extrapolation.
mechanism: Two changes, both about the frequency spectrum rather than about position indices. (1) Introduce a RELATIVE position embedding to explicitly maximise 'attention resolution', defined in the paper as a log-base exponential of the smallest discrete positional difference the model can distinguish. (2) Use blockwise causal attention at inference for better resolution. The widely used name 'NTK-aware scaled RoPE' for this work comes from the associated blog post, not from the paper's own title.
speedup_reported: NOT RECORDED. The abstract's quantitative content is empirical language-modelling comparison across interpolation and extrapolation settings, with no speedup, throughput or context-length figure carrying a baseline. This paper is a diagnostic and a method, not a systems result - the durable contribution is the 'attention resolution' indicator.
